questions.question:
**Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

Rapid climate warming in / the tundra biome have been linked / to increasing shrub dominance.

options.text: the tundra biome have been linked

questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"the tundra biome have been linked."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in the part **"have been linked."**
 
• The error in the sentence is related to subject-verb agreement.
 
• The subject **"climate warming" **is singular, so we must need a singular helping verb with it.
 
• We must use** "has" **instead of **"have." **
 
• **"Has"** agrees with the singular subject **"climate warming."**
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

Correct sentence: *Rapid climate warming in **the tundra biome has been linked**__ to increasing shrub dominance.*

questions.solution:

• The use of **"many" **in this sentence emphasizes that there are numerous reasons for the trend of farms adopting automation.
 
• The reason for choosing **"many"** in the blank is to indicate that there are numerous or multiple reasons why farms are increasingly adopting automation.
 
• Using **"many"** suggests a variety of factors contributing to the trend, emphasizing the complexity and diversity of the reasons behind the shift towards automation in farming practices.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

Correct sentence: *Farms are increasingly turning to automation for **many**__ reasons.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Most: "Most"** is used to refer to the majority or a large portion of a group.
 
• **Much: "Much"** is used to refer to a large amount or degree, often with uncountable nouns.
 
• **Little: "Little" **is used to indicate a small quantity or degree, often with uncountable nouns.
